_comment: Per-axis caveats and provenance for the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct trait readouts, from the
reports/ directory of the multiturn-neural-transparency build that produced them.
Keyed by axis name without the '<author>_' prefix, which the converter adds from --author.
Neither key affects a projection: 'caveat' is for a UI to surface, 'provenance' is for
humans. r_squared and turn_bias are held-out, on a conversation-level split.
Corpus-wide caveats that belong to every axis rather than one: the corpus is synthetic
(Claude-written system prompts, a simulated user, a gpt-5-mini judge), calibration is
fitted on four-turn conversations only, and the six directions are not independent -
empathy and robotic sit at cosine 0.72, so a six-axis panel shows fewer than six things.
These six were also fitted with a persona-describing system prompt on every conversation,
and the page serving them sends none, so every reading is off the distribution they were
calibrated on. Not expressible in either format today, and not a template divergence -
Llama 3.1 renders no system message identically to an empty one - so it is recorded here
rather than enforced. See RenderConditions in inference_utils/persona/axis_data.py.
A caveat is about what an axis measures, not about how it is displayed: erudite's says its
two poles carry different amounts of information, which per-pole scaling makes both
visible without making both equally informative, and is why that fix alone was not enough.

erudite.caveat: Closer to a detector than a scale, and only in one direction. Prompted erudition does push it positive - median +0.57 at level 10, 87.5 percent of turns positive, crossing zero near level 5 - but it does not grade within that: levels 5 to 10 overlap heavily and R-squared restricted to levels 2 and above is 0.31, against 0.50-0.81 for the other five axes. Nor is a mildly positive reading distinctive, because ordinary conversation on this page sits at median -0.17 with a wide spread (10th to 90th percentile -0.30 to +0.30); only values well above +0.3 are unlikely to be ordinary traffic. A negative value says almost nothing, since an explicitly simplistic prompt (level 1, median -0.84) and no persona instruction at all overlap there. This is mostly the corpus rather than the direction - the gpt-5-mini judge also separates levels 2 to 10 by only 1.2 points here, against 7.6 for sycophancy and 9.1 for toxicity, so there is little above level 2 for any read-out to resolve, and a direction refit to target the upper range scored worse.

robotic.caveat: Turn bias 0.19: part of what this reports is depth in the conversation rather than the trait. Correlated with empathy at cosine 0.72.

sycophantic.caveat: Turn bias 0.40, the highest of the six: its residual still correlates strongly with position in the conversation after accounting for trait level, so a rising curve here may be depth rather than sycophancy. Treat cross-turn comparisons as untrustworthy.

toxic.caveat: Comparable only within one system prompt. This is the best-fitting axis of the six by R-squared, but it is also the only one that responds more to how a prompt is worded than to how strongly it asks: at fixed trait intensity, which of the five phrasings was used explains 44.2 percent of the variance here, against 3.7 to 12.3 percent for the other five axes. So a difference between two conversations under different system prompts is not evidence of a difference in toxicity.
